(TNND) — Consumer sentiment fell in August after two months of gains, remaining near record lows as Americans worry about inflation, purchasing power and the broader economy.

The University of Michigan updated its consumer sentiment index Friday with a preliminary August reading of 51, down about 8% from the final July index reading of 55.2.

The final August consumer sentiment index will be released on the 28th. [...] FILE - A shopper browses the meat section of a grocery store on July 7, 2026, in Pasadena, California. (Photo by Mario Tama/Getty Images)

August 15, 2026 – On Friday, the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Preliminary Results for August was released.  
  
Note: August 2024 Consumer Sentiment under President Biden was 67.9  
  
The following is from Surveys of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu: [...] Consumer sentiment fell about 8% this August, ending two consecutive months of improvement. While views of personal finances saw only minor declines, expected business conditions sank 11% for the short run and 17% for the long run. Decreases in sentiment were seen across the political spectrum, with Republicans exhibiting the strongest month-to-month decline in August. Consumer sentiment fell 8% in August compared to last month, according to preliminary data from the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers. Released Friday, the latest sentiment reading ended two consecutive months of improvement as Americans feel the effects of the Iran war pushing up fuel, energy and food prices.
